provenance: Curated local fixture for QueryForge regression evaluation; no uploaded user data.

records.question: List every employee name and salary.
records.reference_sql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY employee_id;

records.question: Which employees earn more than 100000?
records.reference_sql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > 100000 ORDER BY salary DESC;

records.question: Show Engineering employees.
records.reference_sql: SELECT name, title FROM employees WHERE department_id = 10 ORDER BY employee_id;

records.question: How many employees are there?
records.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM employees;

records.question: What is the average salary?
records.reference_sql: SELECT AVG(salary) AS average_salary FROM employees;

records.question: What is the highest salary?
records.reference_sql: SELECT MAX(salary) AS highest_salary FROM employees;

records.question: What is the lowest salary?
records.reference_sql: SELECT MIN(salary) AS lowest_salary FROM employees;

records.question: What is the total salary expense?
records.reference_sql: SELECT SUM(salary) AS total_salary FROM employees;

records.question: How many employees are in each department?
records.reference_sql: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM employees GROUP BY department_id ORDER BY department_id;

records.question: What is the average salary in each department?
records.reference_sql: SELECT department_id, AVG(salary) AS average_salary FROM employees GROUP BY department_id ORDER BY department_id;

records.question: Which three employees have the highest salaries?
records.reference_sql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 3;

records.question: Which employees were hired after 2021?
records.reference_sql: SELECT name, hire_date FROM employees WHERE hire_date > '2021-12-31' ORDER BY hire_date;

records.question: Which employees have a name beginning with A?
records.reference_sql: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE name LIKE 'A%';

records.question: Which employees are in department 10 or 30?
records.reference_sql: SELECT name, department_id FROM employees WHERE department_id IN (10, 30) ORDER BY employee_id;

records.question: Which salaries are between 90000 and 120000?
records.reference_sql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary BETWEEN 90000 AND 120000 ORDER BY salary;

records.question: Which employees are in Sales or Design?
records.reference_sql: SELECT name, department_id FROM employees WHERE department_id = 20 OR department_id = 40 ORDER BY employee_id;

records.question: Which engineers earn at least 100000?
records.reference_sql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE department_id = 10 AND salary >= 100000 ORDER BY salary DESC;

records.question: List unique job titles.
records.reference_sql: SELECT DISTINCT title FROM employees ORDER BY title;

records.question: Which departments have more than two employees?
records.reference_sql: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM employees GROUP BY department_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 2;

records.question: Show each department name and its employees.
records.reference_sql: SELECT d.department_name, e.name FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.department_id = e.department_id ORDER BY d.department_id, e.employee_id;

records.question: Which employees work in New York?
records.reference_sql: SELECT e.name FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.department_id WHERE d.location = 'New York' ORDER BY e.employee_id;

records.question: What is the average salary by department name?
records.reference_sql: SELECT d.department_name, AVG(e.salary) AS average_salary FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.department_id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.department_name ORDER BY d.department_name;

records.question: Which department has the largest budget?
records.reference_sql: SELECT department_name, budget FROM departments ORDER BY budget DESC LIMIT 1;

records.question: Which employees earn more than their department budget divided by ten?
records.reference_sql: SELECT e.name FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.department_id WHERE e.salary > d.budget / 10 ORDER BY e.employee_id;

records.question: Which departments have an employee earning over 150000?
records.reference_sql: SELECT DISTINCT d.department_name FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.department_id = e.department_id WHERE e.salary > 150000;

records.question: Which employees earn more than the company-wide average?
records.reference_sql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees) ORDER BY salary DESC;

records.question: Return the names of employees in departments with a budget above 700000.
records.reference_sql: SELECT e.name FROM employees e WHERE e.department_id IN (SELECT department_id FROM departments WHERE budget > 700000) ORDER BY e.employee_id;

records.question: How many employees are not in Finance?
records.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM employees WHERE department_id <> 30;

records.question: What are the total salaries for departments 10 and 20?
records.reference_sql: SELECT department_id, SUM(salary) AS total_salary FROM employees WHERE department_id IN (10, 20) GROUP BY department_id ORDER BY department_id;

records.question: Show department names whose average salary is at least 110000.
records.reference_sql: SELECT d.department_name, AVG(e.salary) AS average_salary FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.department_id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.department_name HAVING AVG(e.salary) >= 110000 ORDER BY average_salary DESC;
